declarations.normative_text: A statement that changes what a project operator or agent asks, surveys, writes, validates, files, dispatches, trusts, closes, publishes, or does when a capability is missing is behavior-deciding and belongs in this body.
References may elaborate a registered declaration or hold non-deciding measurements and examples; they must not be the only source of a behavior decision.

References use strict dialect version 1: only closed column-zero fences and valid same-line comments can exempt text; tabs, blockquotes, indented code, raw HTML, nested lists, and ambiguous structure are refused.

Follow the active host's discovered project instructions and approval policy; treat AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and MEMORY.md as project context rather than claims that the host loaded any particular capability.

Use only the current session's real connector and operations; if none is available, preserve the reviewed draft or outbox intent, report the pending synchronization to the owner, and never invent a receipt, ticket reference, or confirmation.
Installing this skill never provisions accounts, copies credentials, changes permission or model defaults, or grants a worker coordinator authority.

Use `HANIG_PROJECT_DIR` and declared `HANIG_SKILL_DEP_ROOTS` only to locate the loaded project skill and its required swarm sibling; an `--only` installation must include `hanig-swarm` in the same prefix, arbitrary agent stores must never be searched, and project, plan, state, input, and output paths remain relative to the project directory.
Run survey, interview, plan, ticket drafting and approval, dispatch, tracker drain, and evidence report in that order; each step's output is the next step's input.
Run `survey.py` and read its results before speaking; never ask for a fact the host, repository, or survey can answer.
`truncated` and `stuck` are not the same fact: treat counts from any state other than `complete` as FLOORS, and name `stuck_at` instead of planning as if the count were complete.

Read `allow_accounts`, `deny_accounts`, partition QoS and `qos_grptres`, and `max_mem_per_cpu_mb` before sizing work; `unknown` is never `unrestricted`, so report an unknown state instead of silently planning around it.
For a half-finished repository, read its README, CONTEXT.md, MEMORY.md, architecture decisions, recent history, and existing outputs before proposing remaining work.

For a discovered repository and remote: Adopt it. Do not ask. State the adopted remote and branch in one line before moving on. For a repository without a remote ask once whether and where to push, because staying local is a first-class answer; for no repository ask once whether source must outlive the attempt and recommend nowhere.

A repository is justified only when something must outlive the attempt directory as SOURCE; compute artifacts are data, reach shared paths only through promotion with a named approver, and nothing in this workflow may commit a swarm output to a repo.
Creating a repository is outward-facing and requires the same explicit stop-and-ask gate as tracker filing unless the request contains the literal phrase `swarm autopilot`.

Use `grill-with-docs` when installed, otherwise ask one recommended-answer question at a time only about judgment inspection cannot settle: done criteria, scientific claim, discardable work, budget, protected destinations, and retry exposure.
Ask the most work the owner is willing to repeat after one interruption and use that answer to set the retry boundary; never infer it from the DAG or scheduler.

Stop when the plan can RUN, not when questions run out: use `swarm.py schema` to enumerate every dispatch value, and if a value is still a placeholder, that is a QUESTION, not a detail to settle later.

Ask how often the owner wants a report while the run lasts -- hourly, at each unit's close, only when something needs them, or at the end -- recommending hourly while units are live. Capture cadence and escalation separately: "only at the end" is a legitimate cadence and never a legitimate escalation policy, and a NEEDS_HUMAN unit, an exhausted budget, a blocked merge or a conflict a machine must not settle reaches them regardless. Record both in the plan as a top-level `reporting` block, never in a session's memory, because a session dies and its successor inherits the plan rather than the conversation. It sits outside `plan_digest`, so changing cadence mid-run needs no --accept-plan-change. Nothing enforces cadence; the orchestrator honours it, and enforcing it is ARC-691's clock rather than a sentence here.
Declare every path, glob, and configuration file a command reads; empty inputs, placeholders, and globs matching nothing are refused.

Declare a surveyed partition and account per scheduled unit: validation refuses a nonexistent partition by name and known allow/deny mismatches, stays silent on unknown account data, and cannot check whether the account string exists, so report unknown account data and remember that a typo may pass validation and fail only at submission.
Anything that must reach a shared path needs `promote_to` and a named approver; unit outputs remain relative to the exclusive attempt root.

Ask for and declare `provider` and an explicit `mode` on every code unit. The owner must choose unattended autonomy or deliberate default-permission stalling; confirm the selected provider's exact mode spelling from `paseo run --help` or the provider before writing the plan, record the choice, and pass it verbatim. Mode has no portable or exhaustive positive set; the coordinator does not validate the mode against an exhaustive provider set, so clean validation is no evidence the value is supported and an unsupported value may fail only at provider dispatch. Permission bypass must never be chosen silently, and `bypass` is Claude's spelling and Codex rejects it.
Every code unit must name `repo` and the pull request destination as `target_branch`; the coordinator owns the source branch and legacy `branch` is not a fallback.

Declare each `slurm` and `pipeline` unit's runtime resolution, entrypoint, probe, and verification; a canary must use the same runtime, verbatim probe, partition, and account and be a DAG ancestor, while `runtime: none` is an explicit claim.
Any unit with `max_attempts` above 1 must declare `retry.max_lost` in a metric capped by plan-level `retry_limits`; size the unit from the owner's accepted repeat exposure.
Supply `--mem` when the survey reports `mem_flag_required`; when no survey fact was recorded, the planner remains responsible for the correct cluster flag.

After reading both allow and deny states, ask the owner whether CPU-only work may run in an exclusively allowed idle partition and recommend yes when the shared queue is capped; a named denial is not a question, so say the partition is closed to the account and move on, while an unknown allow or deny state must be reported instead of asked around or used for a recommendation.

Apply `ceil(mem_mb / max_mem_per_cpu_mb)` when the limit is set, quote the resulting charged CPU count, recommend shrinking per-job memory until the charged count is one the account can hold, and ask whether that footprint fits the budget and queue.
State that surveyed `qos_grptres` covers only partition QoS and that account or association QoS may impose an unseen `GrpTRES`; `unrestricted` is not a promise that the job will run.
Ask whether the project has findings to publish. Not every project has any, so do not require `findings.json` when the deliverable is an artifact or merged code change.
Define units by declared outputs and size them by accepted retry exposure rather than presentation stages or command shape.

Judge `slurm` by Slurm accounting plus declared outputs, `pipeline` by launcher exit plus declared outputs, and `code` by agent lifecycle plus outputs plus a produced commit, each over the coordinator-pinned pre-dispatch artifact basis; closure remains a separate by-kind decision.
A `slurm` command is the work itself and must never invoke `sbatch` or `srun`; scheduler options belong in `sbatch` fields.
A `pipeline` command is the workflow-engine invocation and requires fresh work and publish directories.

The coordinator submits a code unit through `paseo run`; the unit uses `prompt`, never `command`, and provider, mode, model, thinking, and environment are fields rather than flags embedded in the prompt.
Every unit output is relative to its attempt run directory; use `SWARM_UNIT_DIR` when a tool needs an absolute path and `promote_to` for shared publication.
The default code agent is `codex/gpt-5.6-sol` with `thinking: high`; overrides belong on the unit, `thinking: null` suppresses the option, and mode remains explicit and provider-specific.
A `slurm` unit must not combine `--array` with declared outputs; use one unit per shard or a separate merge unit over per-task paths.

Build `plan.json` from `swarm.py schema`: every unit declares `id`, `kind`, and `outputs`; `slurm` and `pipeline` declare `command`, while `code` declares `prompt`, plus dependencies, budget, write scopes, and surveyed scheduler flags as applicable.
Treat `write_scopes` as planning metadata rather than process isolation; concurrently runnable code units need disjoint scopes or a dependency.
Rely on the coordinator's verified per-attempt Git worktree for code-path isolation, not `write_scopes`; worktrees isolate paths rather than Unix principals.

Never overwrite an existing PLAN.md, MEMORY.md, or README.md when adopting a repository; write the swarm plan to `.swarm/PLAN.md` when the survey reports protected documents and tell the owner that the protected document caused the redirect.
The human PLAN.md must state what is being built, which interview decisions were made and by whom, and what is deliberately out of scope.
Always run `swarm.py validate plan.json` before ticketing or dispatch and resolve every refusal rather than learning coupled fields one dispatch at a time.
Default tracker work to team `Arc` without asking, and override it only when the owner explicitly directs another team; never use a Slurm account name as a tracker team.
Draft tracker work without network access on the shared login-node coordinator; tracker credentials and remote operations stay in the authorized connector session.
Draft all tracker objects without network access, show the project and every issue title plus the count, and create nothing until one named explicit approval is recorded.

Only the literal request phrase `swarm autopilot` bypasses the tracker approval stop for the whole run; ordinary assent does not count, and a recorded approval is not re-requested after rebuilding a draft.
After approval, create the project then issues, persist every returned id and identifier, and update objects keyed by unit id on later runs rather than duplicating them.
The blockedBy interface is append-only without explicit removal: apply every `add_blocked_by` and `remove_blocked_by` relation, then read all edges back and provide them to the next draft.

A tracker edge read-back must include every issue, using an empty list for a known absence; without a read-back, removals remain `null`, and once filing occurred `check` treats that unknown state as drift.
Describe connector read-backs and outbox receipts as attested rather than verified, and never claim synchronization without naming the read time and source.
After apply and read-back, re-draft and run `tickets.py check` until both unit mapping and blocker edges agree.
Run `swarm.py run plan.json --dry-run` before live dispatch, then schedule `advance` with cron or a Paseo schedule; overlapping advances rely on the coordinator's OS lock.
Let issue state follow coordinator unit state and never the reverse; tracker outages must not alter swarm state.

Refuse any close intent without authorized closing evidence; report an issue closed without it as an integrity violation and reopen it rather than acknowledging the intent because the tracker looks done.

Close `slurm` and `pipeline` issues only on predicate receipts; a code receipt authorizes only opening or linking a PR, and a code issue closes only on the matching merged pull request. Tracker acknowledgments and merge observations are attested, never verified.
A `block` intent means an upstream unit will not complete; the applying session must name that upstream unit.

Apply each pending intent through the connector before marking it applied, and record its outbox receipt only after tracker confirmation; an absent receipt means `unacknowledged`, never that the issue was not filed, and false acknowledgment is worse than missing acknowledgment.
Use each intent's idempotency key so repeated drains are safe.
A run is not finished until `report.py` produces an evidence report; publish its fragment and give the owner the artifact link.
Assemble reports only from plan, coordinator state, and receipts; never add a fact from narrative recollection when it is absent on disk.
Report artifact digests, every receipt's stated limits, and project findings as unverified project claims; never drop a basis hedge while presenting DONE.
A unit that emits `findings.json` must declare it as an output and must also declare `promote_to` for the project directory so the report can read the promoted file.

Write actionable findings that state the measured bound, what the evidence does not prove, and deliberate omissions with the reason for each; never turn a sample with no observed defects into an unbounded no-defect claim.
On adoption, draft remaining units with outputs, check existing outputs before filing, and never turn a completed item or an artifact-free TODO into a unit.
